key_insight: Instead of hand-crafting test-time scaling (TTS) heuristics, AutoTTS frames TTS as an environment-driven discovery problem and uses agentic LLMs to automatically explore and discover effective computation-allocation strategies at inference time.
problem_solved: Manual TTS strategies are heuristic, limited by researcher intuition, and leave much of the computation-allocation design space unexplored; this paper automates discovery to find better, generalizable TTS policies.
method: Reformulate TTS as an environment-driven search where the environment provides tasks, costs, and rewards for allocation decisions.
Use agentic LLMs to autonomously explore computation-allocation policies (e.g., when to allocate more reasoning steps, voting, or deeper models) and evaluate them in the environment.
Select and refine discovered strategies based on performance and cost trade-offs, producing practical TTS heuristics that generalize across tasks.
impact: AutoTTS automates and broadens exploration of test-time computation strategies, enabling practitioners to boost inference-time performance and efficiency without manual heuristic design.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: environment ↔ agentic LLMs loop showing policy proposals, evaluation, and refinement.
Before/after bar chart: task accuracy and latency/cost comparing handcrafted TTS vs AutoTTS-discovered strategies.
Heatmap/timeline: dynamic compute allocation across tokens or examples illustrating where extra computation is applied.
Icon set: agent (LLM), environment (task suite), reward/cost meter to communicate automated optimization.
paper_title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling
paper_authors: Tong Zheng, Haolin Liu, Chengsong Huang, Huiwen Bao, Sheng Zhang
